title: A Alibi for the Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Paloma Quintana is handed a retainer by a dying client who insists that a murder scheduled for the town's anniversary dinner has not yet happened — and pays her to prove it. Following a cipher embedded in the firm's oldest ledger, Paloma discovers the town's founding families have been settling debts with blood for decades, and her own late father's name appears among the payers. As the anniversary dinner approaches, she must choose between exposing the conspiracy and protecting the one person left who loves her. In the end, Paloma decodes the ledger, confronts the intended killer at the dinner itself, and forces justice into the open — at the cost of her law license and the last illusion that her town was ever innocent.
about_author: K. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town paralegal who spent a decade watching wills reveal more than families intended. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet towns, and the violence hidden in proper filing.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Paloma Quintana, POV. A frail stranger named Edmund Voss arrives at her office with cash in advance and an impossible request: prove that his daughter's murder — dated three days from now — hasn't happened yet. Paloma almost refuses until Voss mentions her father's name. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into compulsion; she takes the case against every professional instinct.

chapters.title: Filed Under Q
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Searching the firm's archives for anything on Voss, she finds a ledger older than the practice itself, its margins dense with numbers that don't balance. Her mentor, Ruth Calloway, warns her off with unusual fear. Beat: dread; the first cipher fragment surfaces — dates matching unsolved disappearances across ten years.

chapters.title: A Town That Keeps Its Books
chapters.summary: Alternating between Paloma and Deputy Marisol Reyes, who is quietly re-investigating a cold case the sheriff closed too fast. Paloma interviews the founding families under pretext of estate planning; each alibi is polished, rehearsed, identical in structure. Beat: mounting paranoia — everyone in Bellhaven answers questions with the same script.

chapters.title: The Cipher in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Late-night work reveals the ledger's numbers are a book cipher keyed to the town charter itself: payments logged against names, including her father's, marked 'settled' the year he died. Beat: grief curdling into anger; she realizes the murder Voss predicted may be a debt being collected.

chapters.title: What the Daughter Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol, POV. The deputy digs into Voss's daughter, Elena, an archivist who requested the same charter documents weeks ago and then went silent. Marisol finds Elena alive but hiding, terrified, holding photographs of the ledger pages. Beat: hope with teeth — an ally, and proof Paloma isn't crazy.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The town prepares its sesquicentennial dinner; invitations list every name in the cipher's payment column. Ruth confesses partially: she helped file the ledger years ago believing it was historical record, not a kill-list of obligations. Beat: betrayal and pity intertwined; trust becomes a currency Paloma can no longer spend freely.

chapters.title: Two Days Before
chapters.summary: Marisol, POV. Someone ransacks Elena's hideout; Marisol gets her out barely ahead of a black truck. The sheriff — whose name appears twice in the ledger as both payer and collector — suspends Marisol. Beat: the walls close in; the law itself is compromised, forcing both women outside it.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Decoding the final entry, she learns the target isn't Elena but Voss himself — the man who hired her is paying for his own murder to expose the system from inside his death. Her father 'settled' his debt by taking another's place ten years ago. Beat: devastating reversal; loyalty and truth become the same impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Paloma and Marisol, alternating. At the dinner, Paloma reads the decoded ledger aloud over the toast while Marisol secures Elena's testimony and blocks the sheriff's exit. The intended collector moves on Voss; chaos, a near-killing, and arrest — not by the sheriff's department, but by state troopers Marisol summoned off-book. Beat: climax; truth spoken in a room built on silence.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV, weeks later. The bar revokes her license; the town splits between gratitude and resentment. Voss survives, testifies, and leaves her his estate — which she donates to Elena's archive project. Final scene: Paloma closes the old ledger for good and opens a private investigations office above the courthouse. Beat: bittersweet resolution; justice achieved outside the law, at the price of practicing it.
